FOREWORD

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 30 April 1975, after the draft finalized by the Food Hygiene, Sampling and Analysis Sectional Committee had been approved by the Agricultural

and Food Products Division Council.

0.2 Advertising is vital for successful marketing of food products. It provides an essential service to the consumer, to the industry and Commerce, to the government and the 'economyin general. This is true only when such advertising is truthful, responsible and legal. The present code has been evolved keeping in view the role which advertising plays in ensuring the consumer's right to knowledge about the ~p~cts he buys, and the industry's problems in meeting the demands o~rket forces in the best way possible.
0.3 In the preparation of this standard due considesation has been ~iven
to the Prevention of.Food Adulteration Act, 1954 and the Rules framed thereunder and the I?fuit Products Order, 1955. Assistance has �:bccn derived

from the following publications, International. Podc of Advertising Pr..tcticc, Chamber.:of Commerce, 1966. The :"!lllrrnational

Labelling of Food R<'gllialions No. 400, of the Unitl'd Kingdom, 1970.

1. SCOPE
1.1 This code: lays down basic principles and rules of conduct for rood advertising and claims,

2.5 food Advertlalal- The words food advertisement are construed throughout this code in their broadest sense to embrace any, form of advertising or publicity relating to food. Therefore, it should include all material whether written, pictorial, spoken or film, which features a message promoting a food product, or a food practice.
2.6 Food-Additive - Any substance not normally consumed as food by itself and not normally used as a typical ingredient of the food, whether or not it has nutritive value, the Intcmional addition of which to the food for a technological (including organoleptic) purpose in the manufacture, processing, preparations, treatment, packing, packaging, transport or hold. inA' of such food results or may be reasonably expected to result ( directly or indirectly) in it Of its by-products becoming a component of or otherwise affccti ng the characteristics of such' foods, The term does not include contaminants or substances added to Iocd for maintaining or improving
nutritional qualities.

2.1 IDlrecileat - Any substance. including food additive, used in the manufacture or preparation of food and present in the final product,
2.8 Servlal - A reasonable quantity or food suited for consumption, at one time, by an individual from a specified group of population.

4. RULES

or CONDUCT

4.1 a--If
4.1.1 Food advertisements should be 10 framed u not to abuse the confidence of the consumer or exploit his lack of experience or knowledge. 4.U Food advertisementsshould not p~y on supersti.tion nor shouldthese take undue advantage of beliefs, feelings and weaknesses of the consumers. 4.13 Food advertisement should not hurt religious sentiments of the consumers,

4.2 TftltIaItd PreMatatioa 4.2.1 Food advertisements should not contain any statement or visual presentation which directly or by implication, adds or omits information or causes, ommission or ambiguity which is likely to mislead the consumers. 4.2.2 No claims purporting to be statements of fact should be made if they are likely to mislead.
NO'1'B - Rounded off figures for caloriu. inlredieata etc, could be,iven. provided rounded off lilure does not cUsturb the relevance orthe result claimed.

4.2.3 Food shall not be described or presented in advertising by words, pictorial or other devices including wrapper design, colour and style of lettering which would refer to or are suggestive either directly or indirectly of any other branded food productswith which such food might be confused, or in such a manner as to lead the purchaser or consumer to believe that the food is associated or confused with the food of his choice by mere imitation of brand names, wrapper design or other device.
4.2.4 A misleading food advertisement should not be exoneeated on the grounds that the advertiseror someoneacting 011 his behalf has subsequently provided the consumer with accurate information.

4.2.4.1 Specifically, food advertisements should not misle,d as to: a) the qualities of the product advertised, fur instance, its composition, nutritive value, its utility or suitability, its commercial or geogra.. phical origin; b) the price, quantity and terms of purchase;

c) the services accompanying purchase, inclUdinS' QeljYer)', cesclIADIO

4.2.4.Z Scientific terms, statistics, quotations from technical .llterature and the like should be used with a proper sense of re5JX'ilsibnity� to the consumer. Statistics with a limited validity should not be-presented in such a way as to make it appear that these are universally true.

4.2.4.3 Food advertisements purporting that the purchaseof a product will support some charitable cause should not mislead as to the share of the proceeds which will go to the charity unless quantum 'is specified.

4.3 Te.tIIIloafail aacI ReI.reaces
4.3.1 Testimonials should be genuine and not contain any statement or visual presentation likely to mislead nor should they be used in a manner having that effect. Testimonials which are obsolete or otherwise no longer applicable should not be used. .
4.3.2 Food advertisements should not contain reference to any person, firm or institution without due permission. Nor should a picture of any identifiable person be used in food advertising without due permission.. ~

4.3.3 Food advertisements should not contain any reference to anbdler firm or product which is likely to bring that firm or product into contempt

5.4.3 No food advertisement should, without JUlti6aWe,~,re8Ioft ':.'indttee fear in the consumer that they are suffering, or may,,\yitllOut :t",at~~: or .uffer more severely, from.an ailment, illness ~ disease~, Ii� 5.4.4 No food advertisement should contain any refm'eDce to:.,dOCiE or t hospital'tests, unless suchreference ean ,be lubstantiated "'by, inti,' ' ,ent evidence, and can be properly used in the manner proposed. .',hi,'.110 applies to the use of dress or surrounding in a manner"lik~ly to,�ee.nvey ;8ft impression of independent professional medical advice or reco'nlmendation. 5.4.5 No food advertisement should contain the terms 'college. clinic, institute, laboratory, or similar terms, unless the establishm~nt referred to genuinely corresponds to the description used. s, SPECIAL 'CATEGORIES or ADVERTISING 6.1 AcIYe111" for Sal.. ProlDodoa Selle. . . - Food advertisements which invite the consumer ,to take part in competitions in order to promote sales; food advertisements which offer premiums or gifts to the consumer; and food advertisements which set out other promotion schemes like trading
I

stamps, combined offers, etc, should state clearly all the conditions relating to the scheme advertised. The consumer should not be Jed by such food advertisements to overestimate the value of the offer. 6.2 Mall Order Food Ad"ertt.baI- Special care should be taken in framing mail order food advertlsements, bearing in mind that the consumer usually has no opportunity to inspect the merchandise beforehand. 6.2.1 In particular) such advertisements should contain: a) a clear and accurate description of the product offered (including all information required on the label, such as list of ingredients),

the terms of delivery (including approximate date thereof'), payment and return; , b) accurate information on the identity of the food advertiser, including all details necessary to enable the consumer to get in touch personally with the food advertiser or his representative without any unreasonable delay; food advertisements containing only an accommodation address or a post-office box number should not be accepted; and
c) accurate information of shelf life of perishable commodities should be mentioned in the advertisements.

7.1 ~poa.iblUty 7.1.1 Responsibility for the observance of� thcrulcscfconduct

b) the publisher, medium owner or contractor who publishes or
distributes the advertisement.
7~1.2 Anyone taking part in the planning, creation or publishing of an advertisement should exercise his proper responsibility to ensure that the rules are observed.

1.1.3 This responsibility embraces the advertisement in its entire content and form. including testimonials and statements or visual presentations originating from other sources. The fact that the content or form wholly or in part originates from other sources should not be an excuse for nonobservance of the rules. No advertiser, advertising practitioner or agent, publisher, medium owner or contractor should publish any advertisement which has been found unacceptable by a well-defined section of the population,

7.2 IaterpretatioD
1.%.1, The rules of the code should be applied in the spirit as well as in the letter. Owing to the different! characteristics of the various kinds of media (press, television, radio, posters, films, etc), a -presentation which may be acceptable for one medium may not necessarily be acceptable for another. 1.2.2 Food advertisements should be judged by their presumed impact on the consumerJ : bearing in mind that the consumer is usually motivated by impressions gained from a brief scanning, of the advertisement in its , m~~~ , ! l
